principles.text: Never increase risk per trade to revenge-trade out of a drawdown; in a drawdown you should reduce size - chasing losses with bigger positions is how he turned 0.5% risk into a 35% drawdown.
When you get stopped out of 5+ dip buys in a session, the market is telling you to take a step back and trade less for a while.
Drawdowns are unavoidable and you are in one most of the time; even the biggest winners (e.g. NVIDIA) spent years in drawdown - judge yourself on process, not a perpetual all-time-high equity curve.

Strike a balance between holding winners and protecting profit by knowing your own temperament: if seeing profits stripped away frustrates you, sell more into strength and accept giving up some upside.
A good entry is confirmed by what happens after you exit: if a stopped-out trade keeps going against you, the stop was effective and the entry was sound.
After a red day followed by a gap up, a pullback on the gap-up day can be a buy rather than something to avoid - watch the fade after the opening range.
His edge has drifted from pattern/setup classification toward discretionary reads of theme and general market - in a fast market a clean tight-range breakout often is not available.
